calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Islanders
calls.body: On depth, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.

surprises.head: Toronto brought the hits
surprises.body: Toronto usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 160 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 89 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: The Maple Leafs end a nine-game winless run
paras: The Maple Leafs won for the first time in ten games, after going 0-8-1. Anthony Duclair struck first for the Islanders early in the first. The Islanders’ Kyle Palmieri left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was placed on injured reserve. Mathew Barzal made it 2-0 for the Islanders early in the period, but they didn’t score again. Dakota Joshua got the Maple Leafs on the board a little over three minutes later, and Chris Tanev tied it up early in the third. Gavin McKenna put the Maple Leafs ahead for good midway through the period. Easton Cowan added the empty-netter with just under two minutes left to make it 4-2.

The Maple Leafs had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Islanders 32-22. They had six shots in the first period and trailed 1-0, then outshot the Islanders 26-7 the rest of the way. Anthony Stolarz made 20 saves for the Leafs, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 of 31 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Jake McCabe, by our Swing measure.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Maple Leafs improved to 9-14-3 and climbed off the bottom of the Atlantic to seventh, while the Islanders dropped to 11-7-5, slipping to fourth in the Metropolitan.
